history.dynasty: 20th century (present structure); legends traced to 16th century
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. Manikaran Sahib is a Sikh gurudwara in Manikaran, Parvati Valley, Kullu district (not the town of Kullu as the CSV's town column suggests — corrected to Manikaran), famed for its natural hot springs at about 1760 m altitude beside the Parvati River. Sikh tradition says Guru Nanak Dev Ji visited with Bhai Mardana in the 16th century (some sources say 1574 during the third Udasi): with no fire to cook food, he had a stone lifted and a hot spring emerged; langar food is still cooked in the spring water. Hindu legend says Parvati lost her jewel (mani) in the river, Shiva manifested the hot springs to find it, giving the place its name. The present gurudwara was built in 1920 by Baba Narain Hari (one source says 19th century — conflict). It is a shared Hindu-Sikh pilgrimage site. Coordinates are POI-matched from map.geocode.

name: Manikaran Sahib
town_description: Manikaran is a small pilgrimage town in the Parvati Valley of Kullu district, famous for its natural hot-water springs and as a shared Hindu-Sikh holy site on the banks of the Parvati River. It lies about 45 km from Kullu and is close to Kasol.

travel.railway: No nearby broad-gauge rail; Chandigarh is the practical railhead
travel.road: By road from Bhuntar/Kullu via Kasol on Manikaran Road

visitor_information.best_time: Year-round; October to March for pleasant weather
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not verified in sources; gurudwaras generally remain open all day for devotees
